answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making trust a slow-growing resource. Every newcomer starts in a shallow lagoon where its stake is locked and only a thin ripple of earnings is released per epoch. Each identity must serve real work for many epochs before its stake unlocks, and the delta between a newcomer's earning rate and an established agent's widens with time served. Spinning up a hundred fakes means a hundred separate long waits, since waiting is per identity and cannot be bought or run in parallel.
